Does overtime include fringe benefits on certified payroll?

On a Davis-Bacon or prevailing-wage contract, a wage determination sets a required base rate and a required fringe benefit rate for each classification. A contractor can meet the fringe portion by contributing to a bona fide plan — health insurance, a pension, an approved apprenticeship fund — by paying it straight to the worker in cash instead, or by some mix of both. Which one a contractor picks changes the overtime math, and it is a distinction most payroll defaults get wrong.

Under 29 CFR 5.32 and the FLSA "regular rate" definition it borrows from 29 CFR 778.7, a bona fide plan contribution is excluded from the regular rate used to compute overtime. It is owed at the same rate for every hour worked, straight-time or overtime, and never gets a time-and-a-half premium. Cash paid in lieu of fringe is included in the regular rate — it is treated the same as the base wage for overtime purposes, so it does get the premium on hours over 40.

Worked example. A worker's base rate is $28/hr, with $8.50/hr paid into a bona fide health plan and $2/hr paid in cash instead of a plan contribution. On 6 overtime hours, the correct overtime rate is ($28 + $2) × 1.5 = $45/hr. A payroll system that only applies the premium to the base rate — paying $28 × 1.5 + $2 = $44/hr instead — underpays by $1/hr on every overtime hour: $6 for this worker, this week, and it compounds across every classification and every week the same shortcut runs.

Two things this rule does not do:

  1. It does not change how much fringe is owed in total — a bona fide contribution and cash-in-lieu-of-fringe both count toward satisfying the required fringe rate. It only changes whether that portion gets an overtime premium.
  2. It does not apply to fringe that is never actually paid or contributed. A wage determination's fringe rate is a floor on total compensation, not automatically satisfied by naming a plan that receives nothing.

Open the calculator, split this week's fringe into its bona fide and cash portions, and see the correct overtime rate next to what the common shortcut would have paid. Nothing is uploaded.

No warranty. This page is free arithmetic and a plain-language summary of a federal regulation, not legal or compliance advice. It does not replace a qualified payroll or compliance professional, and it does not determine whether a specific contract or plan qualifies as bona fide. Verify every figure and your actual obligation before relying on it. The authors accept no liability for loss arising from its use.

Common questions

Does overtime on a Davis-Bacon job include fringe benefits?

It depends on how the fringe is paid. A bona fide contribution to a health, pension, or apprenticeship plan is excluded from the overtime "regular rate" under 29 CFR 5.32 and 29 CFR 778.7, so it is owed at the same rate for every hour and never gets a time-and-a-half premium. Fringe paid directly to the worker in cash instead of into a plan is included in the regular rate, so it does get the overtime premium on hours over 40. Paying cash-in-lieu-of-fringe at straight time during overtime hours — which is what many payroll systems do by default — underpays every week it runs.

What counts as the "basic hourly rate" on a wage determination?

The wage determination for a classification states two numbers: a basic hourly rate and a fringe benefit rate. The contractor must provide at least their combined total, through any mix of cash wages, bona fide plan contributions, or cash paid in lieu of fringe. This calculator asks for both required figures and both actual figures so it can check the combined total and, separately, get the overtime math right — the two figures play different roles.

How does the apprentice-to-journeyman ratio work on certified payroll?

A registered apprenticeship program's wage determination sets an approved ratio, such as one apprentice per three journeymen, applied per classification at the site. Apprentices beyond that ratio are not entitled to the reduced apprentice rate — they must be paid the full journeyman prevailing wage for the hours they worked. This calculator reports how many apprentices exceed the approved ratio from the counts you enter; it does not look up the approved ratio for you, since that comes from the specific apprenticeship program's registration.

Does this generate my WH-347 certified payroll report?

Not the signed filing. This page checks one worker and one week; the WH-347 report builder fills the weekly payroll columns for every worker (hours by day, gross, deductions, net) with the same overtime rule and a prevailing-wage check on each row. It does not submit or sign anything on your behalf, and the Statement of Compliance stays yours to sign.

Does this tell me which wage determination applies to my project?

No. The applicable wage determination comes from the contracting officer and the project's own solicitation, published on SAM.gov. This calculator takes the required base and fringe rates as inputs you already looked up — it never guesses a rate or a classification for you.

vs-doing-it-by-hand.html.text:

This calculator vs. doing it by hand

Certified payroll overtime is arithmetic anyone can do with a calculator or a spreadsheet. The problem is one non-obvious rule: cash paid directly to a worker in lieu of fringe counts toward the overtime "regular rate" and must itself carry the time-and-a-half premium, while a bona fide plan contribution never does — and a hand calculation built for ordinary hourly overtime has no reason to know the difference exists.

Where a hand calculation usually goes wrong

StepCommon mistake by handWhat this calculator does
Finding the overtime rate1.5x the base cash rate only, the way ordinary hourly overtime works, with fringe added separately at a flat rate on every hour.1.5x the base cash rate plus any cash-in-lieu-of-fringe, since 29 CFR 5.32 / 778.7 puts the cash-fringe portion in the regular rate.
Bona fide plan contributionsSometimes folded into the same overtime multiplier as cash pay, which overpays the plan contribution unnecessarily.Excluded from the overtime premium entirely and paid at the same flat rate every hour, exactly as the regulation allows.
Checking the wage-determination minimumCompared against base rate alone, missing that fringe counts toward the required total too.Compares required base + fringe against actual base + bona fide fringe + cash fringe, and reports any shortfall per hour.
Apprentice-to-journeyman ratioTracked separately, if at all, and easy to miss when a crew's mix shifts mid-week.Reports how many apprentice hours exceed the approved ratio from the counts you enter.
Is anything I enter uploaded anywhere?N/ANo. The calculator runs entirely in your browser; nothing is sent to a server.

Common questions

What's the most common mistake when calculating certified payroll overtime by hand?

Applying the overtime premium to the base cash rate only, and paying any fringe paid directly to the worker in cash at straight time even during overtime hours. Under 29 CFR 5.32 and 29 CFR 778.7, cash-in-lieu-of-fringe is part of the overtime "regular rate" and must itself get the time-and-a-half premium. A bona fide plan contribution is excluded and never gets the premium — the two figures are easy to swap by hand.

Why do payroll systems and spreadsheets get this wrong by default?

Most general-purpose payroll software and hand-built spreadsheets compute overtime as 1.5x the base hourly rate, because that is correct for a plain hourly job with no fringe. Certified payroll on a Davis-Bacon or prevailing-wage job adds a second required figure, the fringe rate, and the rule for which part of it counts toward the regular rate is specific to government-contract wage law — not something a general payroll setup applies unless it was built for this.

Is a spreadsheet formula good enough once it's built correctly?

Only until the mix changes. A formula built for one classification with a fixed split between bona fide and cash-in-lieu fringe silently gives the wrong overtime rate the week a worker's cash-fringe portion changes, or the week someone copies last week's blended rate forward instead of recomputing it from this week's actual pay.

Does this calculator check whether my contract is covered by Davis-Bacon?

No. Whether a contract is covered, which wage determination applies, and a worker's approved apprentice rate all come from the contracting officer's wage determination and the registered apprenticeship agreement. Both a hand calculation and this calculator take those figures as inputs already looked up; neither one guesses them.

Does this generate or submit my WH-347 certified payroll report?

No, and neither does a spreadsheet on its own. This calculator checks the underlying arithmetic — required vs. actual compensation, the correctly computed overtime rate, and the apprentice ratio — for one classification, one week, so you can carry the right numbers into a certified payroll report. It does not know your project name, contract number, or DOL's exact form layout, and it does not submit or sign anything.

Should I use this calculator or LCPtracker?

You type one worker's wage-determination rate, fringe, actual pay, and hours for one week, and it checks the combined-compensation requirement and computes overtime correctly when part of the fringe is paid in cash instead of into a bona fide plan.

LCPtracker's own materials describe a validation engine that flags Davis-Bacon and prevailing-wage errors across submitted certified payrolls before they go to the agency, run against the payroll data a contractor's system feeds into it. This page does one narrower thing directly: given a wage determination's base and fringe rates plus what a worker was actually paid, it computes whether cash-in-lieu-of-fringe was correctly included in the overtime regular rate under 29 CFR 5.32 / 778.7, so you can check that one calculation by hand before it ever reaches a submission system.

Common questions

Is this the official DOL WH-347 form?

No. It fills the same columns as the WH-347 payroll sheet (hours by day, total hours, rate, gross earned on the project, deductions, net) and checks each row against the wage determination you type in. You still sign the Statement of Compliance on the back of the official form or your agency's equivalent. DOL publishes the form and its instructions on dol.gov.

How are overtime hours decided?

Hours over 40 in the workweek are overtime, counting hours the worker put in on other jobs that week, which you enter in the other-jobs column. Those hours are assumed to come first, so overtime lands on this project's hours last. If your timekeeping splits it differently, enter the hours that way and check the result.

Does overtime include fringe benefits?

Cash paid in lieu of fringe is part of the overtime regular rate and gets the premium. A contribution to a bona fide plan does not. Each row applies that rule, and flags the dollars a base-only payroll system would have underpaid.

Do I enter full Social Security numbers?

No. The form asks for the last four digits only, and this page refuses anything longer. Nothing you type is sent anywhere, stored, or put in a link.

What does it leave out?

Which wage determination applies, whether the contract is covered, apprentice registration, fringe plan qualification, the Statement of Compliance and state prevailing wage forms that differ from the WH-347. Rates are what you type.
